newsitem.title: USA: Moody's cuts L.A. Community Bunker Hill to Ba.
newsitem.headline: Moody's cuts L.A. Community Bunker Hill to Ba.

text.p: Effective today, Moody's has revised the ratings on the Los Angeles Community Redevelopment Agency's Bunker Hill Project Area to Ba from Baa1.
The significant erosion of taxable valuation within the Bunker Hill Project Area has resulted in a shortfall of pledged tax increment revenues needed to meet debt service requirements.

Based on fiscal 1997 incremental assessed valuation, incremental revenues will provide only 94% of the revenues needed to meet debt service requirements on the project area's bonds (a shortfall of approximately $2 million).
In addition, the agency anticipates that it will be required to pay almost $4 million of taxpayer refunds in fiscal 1997.
On November 15, the agency deposited $5.7 million with the fiscal agent in order to bridge the gap between projected revenues and project area obligations.

Management reports that, even under a conservative scenario, existing non-pledged moneys (i.e. funds on hand, interest earnings and loan repayments) will provide sufficient resources to ensure complete debt service payments for the next five years.
However, the ability to satisfy project area obligations could be jeopardized by further tax base declines and refunds not anticipated in these projections.

The current rating revision reflects the presence of an ongoing shortfall of pledged revenues (i.e. incremental revenues) which, absent of stabilization and renewed tax base growth, will create a vulnerability as to timely bond payments over the long-term.
The tax increment revenues from the Bunker Hill Project Area secure approximately $309 million of tax allocation bonds.
Approximately $202 million and $65 million of these outstanding bonds are additionally secured by insurance commitments provided by FSA and AMBAC, respectively.
